clue.text: Treated English skinhead for skin eruption

indicators.note: something treated has been processed or worked on, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of skin is S

explanation.surface: A doctor attends to an English skinhead's rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' looks like one person, but it splits as skin + head, the first letter of 'skin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingles is a painful viral rash, a blistering outbreak on the body caused by the chickenpox virus.

clue.text: Tell facts briefly to the marines

parts.note: info is a short form of information, or facts
RM stands for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Briefly pass the facts on to the marines.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform is to give someone news or knowledge.

clue.text: Old British coin found in Africa

definitions.meaning: a former gold coin worth twenty-one shillings

explanation.surface: An old coin discovered somewhere in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The pre-decimal coin worth 21 shillings shares its name with the West African republic whose gold it was minted from.

clue.text: Choose to speak to the voters

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: A candidate decides to address the people at the ballot box.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the whole body of people entitled to vote.

clue.text: Head baker oversees its production

definitions.meaning: in British slang your head, as in 'use your ...', is this word
a baker makes bread in this shape

explanation.surface: The head baker supervises the making of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang treats the head as a bread item ('use your noggin'), and a baker's oven turns out bread in this form.

clue.text: Doubtless pertaining to the turf

definitions.meaning: belonging to a racecourse, the turf being horse racing

explanation.surface: Something is surely to do with horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means certainly; read literally it is 'belonging to the racecourse', the turf being horse racing.

clue.text: Light pine acquired for reasonable price

parts.note: fair means light in colour, as of hair or skin
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Pale pine wood bought at a sensible cost.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAL is softwood timber such as pine, a sense less common outside Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair deal is an equitable bargain, one at a just cost.

clue.text: Urge fellow to become a journalist

parts.note: to press is to urge
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: Someone encourages a chap to go into reporting.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressman is a newspaper reporter, a member of the press.

clue.text: Subordinate not on team register initially

parts.note: a switch that is not on is off
a side is a team in sport

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of register

explanation.surface: A junior player is left off the team sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: OFFSIDER is chiefly Australian for an assistant or sidekick.
explanation.definitionFit: An offsider is an assistant or deputy, someone who works beneath and alongside another.

clue.text: Concerning Anglicans in the past

parts.note: on means about or concerning; the letters of the answer also happen to sit inside this word, a coincidence
CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: A remark about how churchgoers used to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some earlier time.

clue.text: A court I have found to be busy

parts.note: I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone finds a tennis court is busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone busy is occupied and on the go, the opposite of idle.

clue.text: Doctor meeting model in centre of ship

indicators.note: in puts the doctor and model inside the word for centre

parts.note: the core of something is its centre
a vet is an animal doctor
the Model T was the classic Ford car

explanation.surface: A medic meets a fashion model in the middle of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of ship' reads as one phrase, but 'centre' is CORE and 'ship' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A corvette is a small, fast naval escort vessel.

clue.text: Advises scouts' fellow females

definitions.meaning: advises means directs or steers someone
the girls' counterpart to the Scout movement

explanation.surface: Someone counsels the female members of a scouting group.
explanation.definitionFit: To guide is to counsel or steer; Guides are the girls' organisation parallel to the Scouts.

clue.text: Resigns after stalls are dismantled

parts.note: stands are market stalls
down means taken down, dismantled

explanation.surface: A trader quits once the market stalls are taken apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand down is to step aside from a post, to quit office.

clue.text: A bra's vital remodelling requires capital

indicators.note: remodelling means reshaping, so these letters are reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A lingerie redesign needs investment money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money; it is a capital city, of Slovakia.
explanation.definitionFit: Bratislava is the capital city of Slovakia.

clue.text: Accountant gets bizarre dress

parts.note: outre means eccentric or bizarre

explanation.surface: A bean counter acquires an outlandish frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' looks like a noun, a frock; it is the verb, to equip or attire.
explanation.definitionFit: To accoutre is to equip or attire someone, especially for a particular purpose.

clue.text: One certain to be replaced immediately

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: replaced here means put back in a different place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sure to be substituted straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be replaced' rearranges CERTAIN into NATRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at once, in a split second.

clue.text: Credit-card number once used to get protective gear

parts.note: a PIN is the personal identification number used with a card
afore is an old word for before or formerly, so once

explanation.surface: Someone uses their card code to buy safety clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is an apron or overall worn to keep clothes clean.

clue.text: Happy to house sibling in harmony

indicators.note: to house means to hold inside, so sibling goes within the word for happy

parts.note: content means happy or satisfied
sis is short for sister, a sibling

explanation.surface: Someone is glad to give a home to a brother or sister and live peacefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Things consistent agree with each other and fit together without conflict.

clue.text: Pole receives lock under pressure

parts.note: S is the south pole
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A Polish person takes a lock under duress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a Polish person; it is a magnetic pole, S for south.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress means strain or pressure, physical or mental.

clue.text: You start tucking into fish as an experiment

indicators.note: tucking into means pushing inside, so the letter goes within the fish

parts.note: a trout is a fish

indicators.note: start picks out the first letter of you

explanation.surface: Someone starts eating fish to try something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' suggests eating; here it signals putting a letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryout is a test or trial run, such as an audition.

clue.text: Yearn to find a cool-headed man

indicators.note: headed means just the head, the first letter, of cool

parts.note: he refers to a man

explanation.surface: Wishing to meet a calm, level-headed man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cool-headed' reads as calm, but splits as the head of 'cool'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to long for it.

clue.text: Cost of providing alfresco spread

parts.note: alfresco means in the open air, outdoors
to lay out is to spread, as of a table

explanation.surface: The price of putting on an open-air buffet.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlay is money spent, an expenditure.

clue.text: Coteries reassembled in secret

indicators.note: reassembled means put together again in a different way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Exclusive cliques gather again privately.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is known only to a small initiated few, hence private or arcane.

clue.text: His clients can't suit themselves

parts.note: suit means both please oneself and provide with a suit of clothes, which these customers have made for them

explanation.surface: A man's customers are never allowed to do as they like.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothier who makes suits to measure for customers.

clue.text: Are there any grounds for optimism? Hardly!

definitions.text: Are there any grounds for optimism? Hardly!

parts.words: Are there any grounds for optimism? Hardly!
parts.note: an ironic reply to the question, meaning there is very little chance

explanation.surface: A gloomy exchange about prospects.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said sarcastically to mean the chances are slim.

clue.text: Some pupils achieve really good grades constantly

indicators.note: some here means a part of the following words, which hold the letters

explanation.surface: A number of students always get top marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means always, at all times, as in 'ever hopeful'.

clue.text: One group came in previously to get liqueur

indicators.note: came in means entered, so one and group go inside the word for previously

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, previously
the Roman numeral I is one
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A single party arrived earlier for drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed-flavoured liqueur.
